prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
Reform UK’s 2024 Contract argues Britain has been broken by Tory failure and will be bankrupted by Labour. It says record taxes, debt, waste, Net Zero, mass immigration, “woke” capture of institutions, and a small boats crisis have hurt wages, services, culture, and security. Reform UK offers a common-sense alternative: take back control of borders, money, and laws; defend British identity and values; cut waste and taxes; restore law and order; scrap Net Zero; and deliver zero NHS waiting lists.

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration, stop the boats, and enforce swift detention/deportation.
- End NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at the point of use; cut back-office waste and use independent capacity.
- Make work pay: raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 and lift the higher-rate threshold to £70,000.
- Slash energy bills by scrapping Net Zero and green levies; unlock North Sea oil and gas and trial shale.
- Restore sovereignty and accountability across government and public life.

Key policies (first 100 days focus and thereafter)
- Immigration: Leave ECHR; create a new Immigration Department; bar asylum from safe-country arrivals; deport foreign criminals; restrict student dependents; 5-year residency/work test for benefits; an Employer Immigration Tax on foreign hires (exempt essential health/care).
- Slash government waste: stop paying interest on QE reserves; save £5 in every £100 across departments; cut foreign aid by 50%; accelerate post-Brexit deregulation; improve HMRC collections.
- Economy (personal): raise tax thresholds; cut fuel duty; scrap VAT on energy; cut stamp duty; restore VAT-free tourist shopping; limit inheritance tax to estates over £2m at 20%.
- Economy (business): lift corporation tax threshold to £100k; reduce main rate to 20%, then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; abolish business rates for high street SMEs (offset with a 4% online delivery tax); simplify the tax code; loosen hiring/firing rules.
- NHS: zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS/social care staff for 3 years; expand training and write off student fees via service; 20% tax relief on private healthcare and insurance; vouchers for delayed NHS access; cut waste, weekend theatre use, and DE&I bureaucracy.
- Net Zero: scrap targets and subsidies; expand oil, gas, SMRs, and other tech; prioritise cheap, secure energy.
- Law and order: 40,000 more frontline police; zero tolerance; tougher sentencing; 10,000 new detention places; end two-tier “woke” policing.
- Education: patriotic, balanced curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; tax relief for independent education; scrap interest on student loans; defend free speech at universities; expand PRUs.
- Benefits: stricter assessments; two-strike job offer rule; focus on young adults; incentivise apprenticeships.
- Brexit: scrap retained EU law; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the TCA; protect UK defence autonomy.
- Defence: raise spending to 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rise; protect forces from lawfare; create a Veterans Department; rebuild defence industry.
- Housing: fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals for social housing; scrap Section 24; drop the Renters’ Reform Bill; protect leaseholders.
- Families: transferable marriage allowance; front-load child benefit; mandate single-sex spaces; curb social media harms.
- Transport/utilities: scrap HS2; end ULEZ/LTNs and 20mph overreach; invest in regional links; new 50/50 public–pension fund utility model; cap standing charges.
- Agriculture/fishing: boost farm budget; scrap climate farming subsidies; “Buy British”; police UK waters; ban foreign supertrawlers; rebuild processing.
- Pensions/social care: Royal Commission; end offshore care-home tax abuses; fix mineworkers’ pensions.
- Constitution/culture: leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; scrap the Equalities Act’s DE&I regime; free speech bill; reform/scrap BBC licence fee; reject WHO treaty/WEF influence; oppose CBDC; celebrate St George’s/St David’s Days; anti-corruption unit.

Funding
- Claimed annual savings: £150bn plus £10bn from extra growth = £160bn.
- Annual costs: £141bn.

TEXT_C:
The Green Party’s manifesto offers a hopeful, science-led plan to tackle the intertwined crises of living costs, inequality and climate breakdown, replacing failed market dogma with fairness, public investment and democratic control.

Core promise
- A rapid, just transition to a zero‑carbon, nature‑positive economy that delivers warmer homes, better public services, secure jobs and lower bills—funded by fair taxation on extreme wealth and pollution, and by borrowing to invest.

Health and care
- Rebuild a fully public NHS, end privatisation and pay staff fairly; cut waits via investment in hospitals, primary care, dentistry and mental health; expand diagnostics; a National Cancer Plan.
- Free personal care for older and disabled people; a funded workforce plan and fair pay; £20bn a year for social care.
- Dignity and rights for disabled people, children in care and unpaid carers.

Homes
- 150,000 new social homes a year; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions.
- Passivhaus‑level standards for new builds; a ten‑year, council‑led retrofit with grants and property‑linked finance to slash bills and emissions.

Energy
- No new oil and gas; end fossil subsidies; a rising carbon tax; wind supplying ~70% of electricity by 2030; unleash solar and onshore wind; community ownership; grid/storage upgrades.
- Stop new nuclear and phase out existing reactors.

Fairer economy and tax
- Average £40bn a year green investment in energy, homes, transport, industry, nature and water; bring rail, water and the Big 5 retail energy firms into public ownership.
- Wealth tax on assets over £10m; align capital gains and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance tax; clamp down on avoidance.
- Support SMEs via regional mutual banks and grants; shift to a circular, repair‑and‑reuse economy.

Work and incomes
- Repeal anti‑union laws; a Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage (support for small firms); 10:1 pay ratios; full rights for gig workers; move toward a four‑day week.
- Immediate anti‑poverty measures: +£40/week to Universal Credit; scrap two‑child cap and five‑week wait; uplift disability and carers’ benefits; protect pensions; pathway to Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature; 30% of land and sea protected by 2030; public ownership of water; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam.
- End destructive fishing in MPAs; phase out factory farming, cages and routine antibiotics; ban blood sports; new Animal Protection Commission.
- Triple farm support for agroecology; cut pesticides; boost UK horticulture; free school meals and breakfast clubs.

Education
- Free, inclusive education; scrap tuition fees and restore grants; £8bn for schools and £5bn for SEND; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; expand childcare; counsellors and school nurses.

Transport
- Public transport renaissance: nationalise rail; free buses for under‑18s; major bus, rail, cycling and walking investment; halt new road‑building; rapid EV transition with scrappage; 20mph default in built‑up areas; frequent‑flyer levy and no short‑haul flights where rail is viable.

Democracy and rights
- Fair Politics Act: proportional representation, end voter ID, curb big money, elected second chamber, votes at 16; empower local and devolved governments; defend human rights and trans rights; end Prevent and hostile environment; humane asylum with safe routes and right to work.

Global justice and peace
- Back Ukraine, international law and climate justice; immediate ceasefire and recognition of Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; restore aid to 1% GNI and increase climate finance; path to rejoin the EU (customs union first); sign the Nuclear Ban Treaty and cancel Trident; reform NATO toward de‑escalation and no‑first‑use.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_D" | "TEXT_C"
}
